gbs-reservoir-experiment-over-400-modes: Abstract, p.1, and Section I, p.2: the paper states its own scope (a >400-mode frequency-multiplexed GBS as the reservoir, benchmark tasks including vowels and MNIST). Methods V A (p.15) gives about 430 supermodes.
reservoir-three-stages-description: Section I, p.2: the paper's own description of its apparatus in three stages (squeezed-light generation, programmable frequency-domain beamsplitter, frequency-resolved photodetection for mean photon number and two-body correlations). The value matches the full sentence, not only the quoted part.
four-classification-tasks-described: Section I, p.2: the paper states its benchmark scope (two synthetic tasks, two real-world tasks: spoken vowels and handwritten digits). Sections III A and III B match.
time-independent-data-qelm-description: Footnote 6, p.2: the paper states that its experiments are on time-independent data only and that it uses 'QRC' as the more general term.
slm-pixels-vs-effective-100-dimensions: Section II, p.5 and Methods V B (p.16): 1920 SLM pixels, about 100 independently controlled modes, MNIST with 100-dimensional vectors is the largest input. The paper states this itself.
camera-512-pixels-5000-frames: Section II, pp.4-6: 512 camera pixels, and 5000 frames to compute mean and covariance (chosen to balance noise against experiment time). Section III B changes the frame count for the vowel scaling study, which the value covers by 'unless noted'.
mean-field-vs-covariance-feature-definit: Section II, p.6: the paper defines the mean-field vector and the covariance matrix (Eq. 1 and the sentences after it) and says what information each holds.
classical-sources-differ-in-bandwidth: Section II, p.6: the authors state they could not match the spectra and bandwidths of the classical sources to the squeezed source. A limit on their own comparison. True type: a limit on a measured comparison (result_type 'setup' stands, no change needed).
synthetic-datasets-setup: Section III A, p.8: 600 points, 4 and 5 classes, scikit-learn moons and blobs, 90 percent train and 10 percent test.
covariance-feature-selection-counts: Section III A, p.8: the paper states the 512 x 512 covariance size, the feature selection, about 10,000 (squeezed) and 30,000 (supercontinuum) selected features, and diagonal-only for coherent and thermal. Appendix D (p.24) says 'top 15,000'; see the anova item for that conflict. This item is as the main text states it.
photon-budget-matched-across-light-sourc: Section III A, p.8 and Appendix A (p.21): power and frame counts were adjusted so that average total detected photons match across inputs; Appendix A gives the per-source counts for moons and blobs.
vowel-dataset-and-encoding: Section III B, p.9: 7 classes, 12-dimensional features, 37 examples per class, 259 samples, generic encoding. Methods V B (p.16) agrees.
mode-removal-by-poisson-noise-substituti: Section III B, p.10 and Appendix C: the paper states the Poisson-substitution procedure for emulating fewer modes. The value stays within the paper's own description of the procedure.
mnist-setup-pca-100-components: Section III B, p.11: PCA to 100 components, 300 samples per digit, 5000 EMCCD frames, average total photon count 3.6 x 10^5.
optical-loss-prevents-quantum-attributio: Section IV B, pp.13: the authors state the loss was high enough that the correlations could in principle come from a classical source, so the better accuracy cannot be ascribed definitively to quantum nature. A limit on their own result.
open-challenge-gbs-qrc-advantage: Section IV F, p.14: the authors state their work does not address whether a GBS-based QRC could beat all classical methods, and that an efficient, not-classically-simulable design is an open challenge.
simulability-because-only-two-body-corre: Section IV F, p.14: the authors state their system is likely efficiently simulable classically, especially because they only measure mean fields and two-body correlations. It is a hedged limit with citations [13], [62], stated by the authors about their own system; no proof here.
data-and-code-on-zenodo: Data and Code Availability, p.14: experimental data and code to replicate the figures are at a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.15288036).
transmission-sixty-percent-not-all-state: Methods V A, p.15: overall transmission about 60 percent, extra phase-modulation loss up to 20 percent, so not all states show squeezing below shot noise at the camera. The paper states this limit on its own apparatus.
camera-measures-average-not-single-frame: Methods V A 2, p.16: the EM gain process is stochastic, giving the average photon number per pixel but not the photons in a single frame. The paper states this property of its own detector.
phase-encoding-generic-100-modes: Methods V B, pp.16-17: pump covers about 40 percent of 1920 pixels, so about 100 modes; each of 12 vowel features maps to 160 pixels; compensating function, Gaussian filter and chirp are identical for all tasks. The scaling factor varies, which the value does not deny.
study-scope-krylov-measures: Abstract, p.1: the paper states which measures it uses and compares (fidelity, spread complexity, Krylov expressivity, Krylov observability, task performance, IPC).
ising-reservoirs-hamiltonian-and-eigenva: Section II, Eq. (8), Table I, p.3: four transverse-field Ising Hamiltonians, h = 0.5, d = 9, 16, 15, 16. Table VI (Appendix E) repeats the d values.
reservoir-readout-dimension-definition: Section II, p.3: the paper defines the readout size N_R = V N_S with V virtual nodes and N_S observables.
simulation-parameters-table-ii: Table II, p.5: N_In = 10,000, N_Tr = 25,000, N_Te = 5,000. Section IV C (p.13) repeats N_Tr and N_Te.
lorenz-task-system-and-sampling: Section II, p.4: Lorenz63 with a = 10, b = 28, c = 8/3, dt = 0.001, down-sampled to 0.02, five-step (0.1) prediction (LXX) and x-to-z cross-prediction (LXZ).
ipc-definition-and-purpose: Section II, pp.4-5, Eqs. (13)-(16): the paper defines the IPC, the Legendre targets and the order sum. The sentence that the IPC does not predict task performance describes how the authors use it; the paper cites other work that uses it for prediction.
spread-complexity-definition: Section III A, p.6, Eq. (25): the paper defines the spread complexity K_S(t) = sum (n+1)|alpha_n(t)|^2 over the Krylov basis.
krylov-expressivity-definition: Section III A, pp.6-7, Eqs. (26)-(27): the paper defines Krylov expressivity through the fidelity of time-evolved states; the bound by the grade m follows from the form of Eq. (27).
krylov-observability-definition: Section III B, p.7, Eqs. (39)-(41): the paper defines the observability of one observable and the sum over K multiplexed observables.
theorem-1-time-evolved-state-in-d-dimens: Theorem 1 (Section III C, p.8), proof Appendix C, p.16, Eqs. (C6)-(C10): grouping the eigenvalue-degenerate components shows |Psi(t)> lies in the d-dimensional span of the xi_p. The proof is direct and complete for this part.
speed-up-excludes-training-cost: Section IV C, p.13: the authors state the matrix-multiplication estimate leaves out the training across thousands of tasks (state-matrix inversion, readout optimization). A limit the paper states on its own cost estimate. True type: a limit on a computed operation count (theoretical), not 'setup'.
random-coupling-six-site-setup: Section IV B, p.12: couplings uniform in [0.25, 0.75], h = 0.5, N_S = 6 sites, all sites measured, V = 10, 30, 50, ten random Hamiltonians per case with mean and standard deviation.
reservoir-setup-lorenz63: Section I, p.1: four reservoirs trained on a chaotic time series, larger reservoirs with random inter-spin couplings, Lorenz63 as the benchmark. Sections II and IV give the details.
two-qgnn-realizations-task: Abstract, p.1: the paper states what it develops and implements (two QGNN realizations for particle interaction simulation).
speculative-qgnn-definition: Abstract p.1 and Section II C (pp.4-5): the paper defines the Speculative QGNN as the model that uses superposition amplitudes directly as classical information to propagate between particles.
implementable-qgnn-definition: Abstract p.1 and Section II D (p.6): the paper defines the Implementable QGNN as the model that passes particle information through RX gate rotation parameters.
cgnn-and-speculative-as-controls: Abstract, p.1 and Section IV D: the paper's own comparison design (CGNN and Speculative QGNN as controls for the Implementable QGNN).
hybrid-division-of-labor: Section I, p.1: the paper states that the quantum part covers encoding, processing and decoding via PQCs, with loss and backpropagation classical.
study-aim-quantum-analog-first: Section I, p.1: the paper states its main pursuit is first to show a quantum analog is obtainable, with performance comparisons after.
qgnn-three-pqc-sections: Section I, p.1: encoder, processor, decoder as parameterized circuits; encoder adds qubits, decoder pools six qubits to two, processor does message passing.
speculative-cannot-run-on-hardware-cost: Section I, pp.1-2: the authors state the Speculative QGNN cannot be directly run on hardware and give the cost estimate: 7 sub-circuits x 1,000 measurements = 7,000 runs per vector, x about 19,000 vectors = 133 million runs per epoch (arithmetic checks). The estimate rests on the stated assumption of 1,000 measurements. True type: a theoretical cost estimate.
speculative-model-extra-subroutines: Section I, p.2: the authors state each run would need a sign-determination subroutine and an expectation-value subroutine, and call this very impractical, hence 'speculative'.
model-based-on-sanchez-gonzalez-graph-ne: Section II A, p.2: the paper states the model it implements follows Sanchez-Gonzalez et al. with encoder, processor and decoder.
classical-gnn-architecture: Section II B, p.4: layer sizes of the classical GNN as listed (8/9, 4/5, 9 and 5, 2), layer normalization, ReLU except the decoder.
data-encoding-amplitude-vectors: Section III A, pp.6-7: node vector size 8, edge vector size 4 with one zero pad, amplitude encoding with Pennylane AmplitudeEmbedding.
encoder-parameter-count: Section III B, pp.7-8: 18 rotation gates, 15 parameters because some share parameters; parameters are the same on every qubit pair.
decoder-and-processor-parameter-counts: Section III B, p.8: decoder unitary has 6 parameters; processor has 16 gates and 8 parameters (two RY columns each followed by cascading CNOTs).
speculative-processor-minimum-five-uses: Section III B, p.8: the algorithm needs the processor at least five times (three edge, two node).
implementable-qgnn-no-qubit-scaling-rela: Section III B, p.8 and Table I caption: the authors state the Implementable QGNN has no obvious scaling with qubit count, because changing qubit count requires an arbitrary experimenter choice of RX gates.
speculative-qgnn-four-qubits-with-memory: Section III C, p.8: the authors state their Speculative QGNN uses four qubits with saved sub-circuit outputs, and that storing the information in extra qubits would be highly impractical, if not impossible.
implementable-qgnn-eight-qubit-layout: Section III D, p.9: qubits 0-3 node states, 4-7 edge states, circuit run 3 times per time step.
edge-count-bounds-three-to-six: Section III D, p.10: three particles with self-edges give 3 to 6 edges; unused RX parameters are zero.
implementable-output-is-expectation-valu: Section III D, p.11: measurement on qubits 2 and 3; expectation values are the predicted x and y accelerations.
training-setup-loss-and-ground-truth: Section IV A, p.11: MSE on acceleration against ground truth from the Taichi Lang particle simulator.
training-setup-optimizer-and-batches: Section IV A, p.11: Adam, learning rate 0.01, batch size 4 (each point a time step), data shuffled each epoch.
processor-count-limited-to-two: Section IV A, pp.11-12: one-processor and two-processor groups; two is the maximum, chosen for the three-particle graphs.
validation-set-size-thirty-percent: Section IV C, p.15: validation set about 30 percent of the training set size.
data-available-on-request-only: Data Availability, p.17: the data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. The paper states this itself; no public archive.
collis-scope-simulator: Section IV D (p.17) and Section V (p.17): three particles in a box, the most basic GNN forms, and a circuit simulator, so real hardware is needed to find any real advantage. The paper states these limits on its own work.
hse-and-css-definitions: Section II, p.2, Eqs. (2)-(3): the paper defines the HSE as the minimum HSD over the convex set C of states of a given separability, and the CSS as the minimizer.
trial-state-parameter-count: Section III, p.3, Eqs. (7)-(10): the trial state is a mixture of s separable pure states with s(2n + 1) parameters (2n angles and one probability each).
destructive-swap-gate-count-and-depth: Section III D, p.4: n CNOT and n Hadamard gates for the destructive SWAP test, depth two with ladder-like connectivity; Fig. 1 shows the circuit.
test-state-assumed-efficiently-preparabl: Section III D, p.4: the paper states the assumption that the test state can be efficiently prepared (direct input or state-preparation methods).
bilevel-optimization-structure: Section III C, p.4, Eqs. (13)-(15): the paper describes the upper-level optimizer (theta, phi) and lower-level optimizer (p).
simulation-setup-and-optimizers: Section IV, pp.5-6: statevector and shot-based simulations, random initial points, GSA upper level, SLSQP lower level.
ghz-ground-truth-analytically-known: Section IV, p.6: the paper states why it chose GHZ states (shows performance; the CSS is analytically known, from Ref. [32]).
n-qubit-xmems-css-not-derived: Appendix A 3, p.9: the authors state they have not derived the CSS of n-qubit X-MEMS and only conjecture its form.
k-css-extension-open-problem: Section V, p.8: the authors state that finding the k-CSS is not straightforward (the 2^{n-1} - 1 bipartition count) and leave the k-CSS and performance improvements as open problems.
consiglio-vsv-exponential-parameters: Section III D, p.4: the authors state the current VSV needs s >= d states (full-rank CSS for entangled test states, found in simulations) and so has exponential parameter scaling. They state it as a limit of their own algorithm. Premise is empirical ('we found'), and it applies to entangled test states; the value does not say so. Stored HIGH stands.
consiglio-vsv-proposal: Abstract p.1 and Section III: the paper states what the VSV is and does (a VQA for the closest separable state under the HSD). Stored HIGH stands.
consiglio-vsv-simulation-scope: The narrowed value matches Section I (p.2) and Section IV (p.5, Fig. 3): GHZ states two to seven qubits with statevector optimization, two to five qubits with shot-based optimization at 8192 shots. The paper states its own simulation scope.
vqa-two-register-proposal: Abstract, p.1: the paper states what it proposes (a VQA for Gibbs states with a PQC on two CNOT-connected registers); Section II defines it.
free-energy-with-entropy-postprocessing: Abstract p.1 and Section II (pp.2-4): the paper's own description of its method (free energy objective, entropy from computational-basis post-processing on one register).
generalized-free-energy-objective: Section II, p.2, Eqs. (3)-(5): the paper defines the generalized Helmholtz free energy and uses it as the objective.
ancilla-register-size-equals-system: Section II A, p.2: the paper's design choice, m = n ancilla qubits for the full Boltzmann distribution without truncation.
ancilla-measurement-gives-boltzmann-prob: Section II B, p.3, Eqs. (8)-(12): the paper derives it step by step (U_A on the ancillae, CNOTs, partial trace gives a diagonal state with p_i = |u_{i,0}|^2; tracing out the system gives the same state on the ancillae). The derivation is complete and short.
pqc-structure-independent-of-hamiltonian: Section II A, p.2: the paper states that the circuit structure does not depend on H, beta or the ansatze U_A and U_S.
entropy-depends-only-on-ancilla-angles: Section II C, p.4, Eq. (15): the entropy term is S(rho_A(theta)), so it depends only on the ancilla angles; the paper states this property of its own objective.
mid-circuit-variant-downside-tfd: Section II D, p.4: the authors state the only downside of the mid-circuit variant is re-use of the ancillae, as for the TFD state.
classical-variant-limits: Section II D, p.4: the authors state that a classical replacement for U_A may give a less expressible distribution and that a shallow, expressible parametrization is non-trivial to find.
fidelity-as-figure-of-merit: Section III, p.5: the paper states it uses the Uhlmann-Josza fidelity as its figure of merit.
ising-ancilla-ansatz-linearly-entangled: Section III, p.6: linearly entangled PQC for U_A with Ry gates and CNOTs.
ising-system-ansatz-parity-preserving: Section III, pp.5-6, Eq. (18) and Fig. 4: parity-preserving brick-wall of R_p gates, each decomposed into two CNOT, six sqrt(X) and ten Rz gates.
ising-parameter-count-table-ii: Table II, p.6: the paper's own tabulated count for its ansatz with l_A = 1, l_S = n - 1 (2n^2 parameters), consistent with Table I's general formula.
ising-circuit-depth-table-ii: Table II, p.6: the paper's own tabulated depth (P + 1)n - P + 4, counting CNOT and sqrt(X) gates, consistent with Table I.
noisy-simulation-setup-guadalupe: Section III B, p.6: ibmq_guadalupe noise model, h = 0.5, one ancilla layer and n - 1 system layers, SABRE transpilation, scaling not following Table II.
barren-plateau-analysis-out-of-scope: Section III B, pp.7-8: the authors state barren-plateau analysis for Gibbs state preparation is beyond the scope of the manuscript.
hardware-run-ibm-nairobi-setup: Section III C, p.8: ibm_nairobi, SPSA, one run per beta for n = 2 and two runs for n = 3, 100n iterations, 1024 shots; noisy simulations used ibmq_guadalupe calibration data.
hardware-fidelity-from-classical-stateve: Section III C, p.8: the paper states the reported Gibbs states came from the optimal parameters found on ibm_nairobi, with the statevector computed classically.
hardware-runs-too-few-to-explain: Section III C, p.8: the authors state the available device time was limited and the number of runs is too low to explain the lower fidelity.
heisenberg-parameter-count-table-v: Table V, p.9: the paper's tabulated count for l_A = l_S = n - 1 (3n^2 - 2n parameters), consistent with Table IV.
heisenberg-circuit-depth-table-v: Table V, p.9: the paper's tabulated depth 3Pn - 3P + 1, counting only CNOT gates, consistent with Table IV.
heisenberg-shot-based-setup: Section IV B, p.9: SPSA, ten runs per beta, 100n iterations, 2n evaluations per iteration, three commuting Pauli sets, 1024 shots, M3 mitigation.
nsb-scalability-open-question: Appendix A, p.13: the authors state that the NSB bias scaling is unproved, that a proof would imply scalable entropy estimation, and that exact diagonalization reached only n = 24.
barren-plateau-analysis-only-qualitative: Appendix C, p.14: the authors state their cost function is not in the form of the cited theory (logarithm in the entropy), so the comparison is qualitative only.
vqa-gibbs-proof-of-concept: Section V, p.11: the authors state the manuscript's scope was a proof-of-concept VQA. Stored HIGH stands.

theory_low.state-matrix-multiplication-count: Section II, p.5, Eq. (18): the 7 + K count (4 for the trace, 2 for exponentials, 1 for the encoded state, K for observables) is stated in two sentences with no derivation. It is an informal operation count, neither a definition nor a proved result. Unlike the circuit-element counts of Consiglio 2024 (fixed by the circuit definition), this tally depends on how the matrix products are carried out.
theory_low.theorem-1-grade-m-equals-d-minus-n1: Theorem 1's second part (m = d - n1) rests on Lemmas 1 and 2 (Appendix C, p.16). Lemma 1 is stated for dimension d and needs a period condition that the statement omits; it is false as written when n1 > 0. Lemma 2's proof replaces exact states by truncated Taylor sums with no error control. The step 'Km and E_{d-n1} are both minimal, so the dimensions agree' is not shown by the lemmas as written. The result itself is textbook-adjacent, but the paper's proof has gaps.
theory_low.theorem-2-liouvillian-grade: Theorem 2 (p.8), proof Appendix D (pp.18-19). The decomposition into transition-frequency terms is sound. The grade claim M = N_omega - N1 rests on Lemmas 3 and 4. Lemma 3 asserts the generalized Vandermonde matrix is invertible 'due to the construction' for any distinct times below the period; that is not shown. Lemma 4 uses truncated Taylor sums with no error control. The proof does not settle the grade identity.
theory_low.lemma-1-eigenspace-space-minimal: Appendix C, pp.16-17. The quoted statement is for dimension d and omits the condition the proof needs (times below the period T_P, and a rescaling of H). As stated it fails when some gamma_p = 0 (then the minimal dimension is d - n1). The conditions are lost in the statement.
theory_low.lemma-2-krylov-space-minimal: Appendix C, p.17. The statement is plain, but the proof is a limit sketch: truncated Taylor sums h_j stand in for the exact states Psi(t_j) with 'epsilon to 0', and the final step ('otherwise Theta would not be invertible') is not a derivation. The proof as written does not settle it.
theory_low.lemma-3-operator-space-minimal: Appendix D, p.18. The proof asserts that the generalized Vandermonde matrix in e^{i omega_P t_j} is invertible for any distinct times below the period 'due to the construction of P'. That is not shown, and it does not hold for every choice of distinct times. The statement is plausible but the proof has a gap.
theory_low.lemma-4-liouvillian-space-minimal: Appendix D, pp.18-19. The proof reuses the truncated Taylor-sum argument of Lemma 2 (Eqs. D5-D7), with no error control, and says only that Theta is 'thus invertible'. A sketch, not a proof.
theory_low.krylov-observability-matrix-multiplicati: Section III B, p.8, Eqs. (42)-(44): the Gram-Schmidt count V K (V K - 1)/2 plus two V K terms is an informal operation count, and the claim r << 1 depends on the assumption N_u >> V K. No proof; the final ratio is also printed inconsistently (see the ratio item).
theory_low.state-matrix-cost-nine-point-nine-millio: Section IV C, p.13, Eq. (52): the arithmetic (7 + 4) x 30,000 x 30 = 9.9 x 10^6 is correct, but it applies the informal count of Eq. (18) to one parameter set. Not a proved result.
theory_low.krylov-observability-ratio-0-75-percent: Section IV C (p.13) prints r = 0.75 percent, but 7380 / 9.9 x 10^6 is about 0.075 percent (0.00075), which is what Section I (p.2) gives. The value holds both figures. 0.75 percent would be two orders of magnitude, not three. The paper's own numbers conflict, and the count rests on an informal formula.
theory_low.expressivity-upper-bounded-by-eigenvalue: Section IV A, p.10: the bounds 9, 16, 15, 16 are the d values of Table I. The paper says the bound 'corresponds to the grade of the Krylov space or the number of pairwise distinct eigenvalues' but does not derive it here; Section III A (p.7) takes m = d from the cited work [35], and Theorem 1's grade part is not settled (see its item). The step from definition to this bound is cited, not shown.
theory_low.two-qubit-xmems-css-derived-kkt: Appendix A 1, pp.8-9: the paper says the CSS was derived by KKT optimization after the VSV hinted at the form, and prints the results (A5)-(A7). The derivation steps are not shown, and the assumed form (A3) comes from numerics. A claim of a derivation, not a proof in the paper.
theory_low.three-qubit-xmems-separability-condition: Appendix A 2, p.9: the paper says the non-negativity condition 'can be rewritten and shown' equivalent to |d|^2 <= b(1-a-b)/9 (A10). The equivalence is asserted, not shown, and the three-qubit CSS form is conjectured from numerics ('we conjecture that the state is not bound entangled').
theory_low.xmems-hse-piecewise-and-bound: Appendix A 3, Fig. 6, p.10: the piecewise form and the limit 2|gamma|^2 (A14) are stated without derivation, and they depend on the n-qubit CSS form, which the paper only conjectures (A11).
theory_low.zero-hse-implies-separable: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section V, pp.7-8: it is an elementary consequence of the definitions (distance zero means equal to a state in C). The paper says 'trivially' and 'immediately' without an argument, and phrases it oddly ('the HSE of an entangled state is zero'). It is also about a calculated, approximate HSE.
theory_low.qga-call-count-estimate: Appendix B, p.10: an estimate that rests on stated assumptions (one million trial states for three qubits, successes proportional to trial states^0.44127) and on a VSV call count of 5 x 10^3 that the appendix asserts without a source; the text says 'even if we take it to be split evenly', which marks it as rough. Not a measurement or a proof.
theory_low.qga-memory-grows-each-success: Appendix B, pp.10-12: the authors' structural argument about the quantum Gilbert algorithm, based on its description in cited work, with no measured comparison.
theory_low.entangling-gates-necessary-ising-boltzma: Appendix B, p.13: the argument by contradiction reaches p0 p3 = p1 p2, then E0 + E3 = E1 + E2, and says only 'which is not in general true for the Ising model'. No computation is shown, and the energy-to-bit-string assignment is not fixed (U_S can permute), so the contradiction is not established. The paper says 'we concluded', a sketch.
